trigger: sshd_config on a normal enterprise or cloud host sets TrustedUserCAKeys and/or AuthorizedKeysCommand (EC2 Instance Connect, SSSD/FreeIPA, Vault/Teleport SSH CA), AuthorizedPrincipalsFile, HostbasedAuthentication yes or AuthenticationMethods
classification_rationale: The product claim 'who can log in over SSH' (YAML, README) is not bounded anywhere: the credential sources the plugin never opens are neither read nor named, and no wire marker says so (required-doc item 6: the plugin README and YAML are the routed row's update obligation).
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. A clean status|list|supported|- with zero key rows was reproduced on the real posix_fs binding for a host whose sshd_config sets all five settings; sshd -T confirmed they are live. Native label MEDIUM; derived I3 (base HIGH) with the I7 raise (conceals a security-relevant limit) governs. Fix direction recorded by the reporter: state the limit in README and YAML, add a presence-only constrained token at global scope, and assert the wire (not a parser flag) in the closure test.

trigger: a macOS home owned by uid < 500 (hidden-account persistence) or a Linux/macOS account whose home is outside /home, /root, /Users (git, jenkins, LDAP homes) holds an authorized_keys file
classification_rationale: Scope exclusion is owner-ruled and README caveat 3 states it, but neither the wire nor the YAML description does, and the YAML overclaims ('every public key in each account's authorized_keys').
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Reproduced with a uid-floor home holding a key file: status|list|supported|-, source|homes|read|0, no token and no row. Mechanical band HIGH (I3 base, I7 raise); the reporter noted it would fall to I7/MEDIUM if the README disclosure were accepted as sufficient. Same fix surface as hp-1.

trigger: a local unprivileged user runs a hung fuse.<custom> daemon with allow_other over ~/.ssh (user_allow_other set); the agent has DAC bypass or the home is 0755; an administrator dispatches list once and the Subscribe stream then drops
classification_rationale: The reconnect teardown joins the command pool unboundedly (agent.cpp:3566) and the plugin has no execute deadline; routed row clause 3 and the #4875 family disclose the hang but not the agent-wide consequence.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Chaos scenario CH-2b (code read; no FUSE host available). Mechanical derivation: I5(c) wedge -> HIGH, E2 raise -> CRITICAL. The wedge root is outside this diff (existing issue #5165: reconnect teardown drains the pool) and the per-plugin half is #4875.

trigger: a subject-run FUSE mount (bare fuse or fuse.<other>, needs user_allow_other) over ~/.ssh blocks open/read forever; the command pool is shared with quarantine dispatch
classification_rationale: Re-framing of the ruled #4875 residual (bare fuse and stacked mounts are guarded by name only); same family as ch-1.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Not verified (no FUSE available). Mechanically HIGH (I5(b) with E2); the reporter recommended no action because routed row clause 3 and the prior ruling carve it out.

trigger: a Linux host whose /proc/self/mountinfo exceeds 1 MiB (dense container node) with a home root, home, Include or key path on a dead network mount
classification_rationale: Routed row clause 3 lists no unreadable-mount-table residual; the oversized read returned nullopt and the whole network-mount guard switched off (only keys:mounts_unreadable said so).
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Also reported as up-4 by the unhappy-path reviewer (an echo: shown the finding). Native LOW; derived MEDIUM (I5, E5) governs. Fix direction: read the table with a larger bound and keep mounts_unreadable for true read failures only.

trigger: any Linux host on systemd 249 or 252 (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, RHEL 8/9, Amazon Linux 2023) where one of the three probed units does not exist, which is every host
classification_rationale: README lists not-found as an observed service state, but on these systemd versions a missing unit prints on stderr only and the runner captured stdout, so the plugin read service:no_output and the listing was permanently CONSTRAINED.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Raised independently by the security-guardian (as sec-2, native LOW, unverified) and the plugin-xplat reviewer (as xplat-1, native SHOULD, verified in Docker on ubuntu:22.04 / systemd 249.11 and debian:12 / systemd 252.39); echoed by five later reviewers. Closes the never-closed code-review r1 SP6. Ordering note from the chaos review: land the scope token with or before this fix.

trigger: a root-authored sshd_config with an AuthorizedKeysFile line of about 100,000 tokens, or about 16,000 glob Include directives re-walking a 4096-entry directory
classification_rationale: Neither the AuthorizedKeysFile token count nor the Include directive count had a cap; only successful reads raised files_read.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Measured: 100k tokens x 512 homes = 5.0 s, 1.6 ms per no-match Include directive; both pin one shared command worker. Root-authored input only, hence native LOW; the derivation table gives MEDIUM (I5, E4).

trigger: a subject-authored authorized_keys of about 2,020 valid lines in an early-sorting home saturates the 2048-row dispatch budget
classification_rationale: README says the listing stops at the row budget; the code charged the saturating file's key rows and then discarded all of them and the file row, so every later account vanished too (drop-all, not first-N). Contradicts code-review r6 F3 ('wasted charge only').
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Verified by probe: zero file or key rows for every account, status constrained with keys:row_cap. Derived MEDIUM (I8, visible not silent; E2 because one account's file decides another's visibility). The reporter flagged that ruling it an audit-evasion control (I1, E3) would make it HIGH; the Architect ruled I8 stands.

trigger: reading the plugin descriptor, README, privilege model, capability matrix, user-manual index and changelog for the shipped unprivileged Linux account
classification_rationale: The descriptor declared Linux SUPPORTED while the README said CONSTRAINED is the common outcome; precedent plugins (printing, mgmt_posture) declare CONSTRAINED; four customer surfaces presented Linux as full.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Raised by plugin-xplat at LOW (I8); extended by the sre and enterprise-readiness reviewers (shown it, so echoes) with new verified evidence: the packaged unit sets NoNewPrivileges=true so a file capability is inert, and the customer-facing surfaces mark Linux full. Merged derivation MEDIUM (I6, I7).

trigger: a packaged .deb/.rpm Linux agent (User=yuzu-agent, NoNewPrivileges=true) whose operator follows the README instruction to put CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH on the agent binary
classification_rationale: The README and the privilege model named a grant that cannot work on the packaged unit and the wrong account name (yuzu, not yuzu-agent); no documented route reaches a non-constrained Linux result.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Verified in Docker (debian:12): a file capability on a binary gives CapEff 0 under NoNewPrivs=1, while an ambient capability gives CapEff 0x4 and reads a root 0600 file. Also raised as ent-1 (guidance half) by the enterprise-readiness reviewer. The packaging half is existing issue #4916.

trigger: an operator reads docs/user-manual/rbac.md and docs/authz-model.md, where the Forensics rows describe only Windows forensic-artefact and app-usage reads
classification_rationale: Required-doc item 5: the permission table the change's contract touches. The sibling plugin extended these rows for itself; this change extended none.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Not raised to HIGH: Forensics is Administrator-only, AdminOrApproval and single-target, and the README, SOC 2 and privilege docs state the identity-material reach.

trigger: systemctl or launchctl cannot be spawned (empty argv or runner spawn_error)
classification_rationale: The README's Result-status table documented an UNAVAILABLE / subprocess_runner:spawn_error row, but the code maps a failed spawn to the CONSTRAINED service:systemctl_unavailable / launchctl_unavailable token and never emits UNAVAILABLE for it. Owning domain agent: cpp-expert.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. The reporter noted an I3 reading for a token-matching consumer; the derived band recorded here is LOW (I8). The README row's own parenthesis contradicts its status.

trigger: an unprivileged agent on the RHEL family (RHEL, Rocky, Alma, Fedora, Amazon Linux), where sshd_config is 0600 root
classification_rationale: README, the privilege model and the YAML header said sshd_config is world-readable and needs no grant; verified on rockylinux:9 and amazonlinux:2023 that it is 0600 root and sshd_config.d is 0700.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Raised independently by docs-writer (as doc-2, likely) and plugin-xplat (as xplat-3, verified). The code is correct: the read is refused visibly as sshd_config:permission_denied.

trigger: a macOS host with Remote Login restricted to specific users: an account holds a key but is not in the com.apple.access_ssh group
classification_rationale: Required-doc item 6: README caveats are the routed row's update obligation; nothing in README, YAML, the matrix or darwin-compat named the pam_sacl login gate (verified locally in /etc/pam.d/sshd).
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Hedged by 'configured, not effective'; no wrong data is emitted.

trigger: default configuration with 0700 homes (the common Linux case)
classification_rationale: README and the privilege model said 'one refused file row per account'; the code emits one per AuthorizedKeysFile entry per account (two by default, asserted by the legs test).
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Wording of two documents against the code.

trigger: a reviewer or auditor reads routed-concern row 22 clauses 2 and 3
classification_rationale: Clause 2 said an unopenable .ssh yields homes:permission_denied (the code emits keys:permission_denied); clause 3 said homes and key paths are checked at the target of their one link hop (only the config path, Include paths and home roots are; homes and keys are refused, never followed).
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. The row is the floor source for this plugin, so it must be exact.

trigger: a root-authored sshd_config whose Include names a dangling symlink
classification_rationale: README promised include:enoent for any dangling config link; the code emits it only for entries a wildcard listing returned, and a literal dangling Include path reads as absent with no token (sshd exits).
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. The output is not wrong; the document over-promised.

trigger: a DSAR or erasure pass reads the response_store inventory row for its list of erasure sources
classification_rationale: Required-doc item 6: the SOC 2 data-inventory rows accrue an entry per consumer of stored results; the sibling plugin's rows are named, this plugin's per-account key fingerprints and home-directory account names were not.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. The adjacent transient-store row and the SOC 2 note already state 'no per-user erasure yet', so none of the I7 categories applies.

trigger: a data-protection or works-council review of the plugin
classification_rationale: Required-doc item 6: the account-name decision (home-directory name, every walked home reported even when keyless) and the cross-host linkability of a key fingerprint were recorded nowhere, unlike the sibling browser_inventory row's dated owner amendment, and the works-council flag the sibling carries was missing.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. The emitter was checked and the minimisation claims are true; the gap is the recorded decision and the works-council statement. The Architect ruled that only the owner's recorded grill choices are quoted, nothing else attributed to him; the owner may reword at the push gate.

trigger: an operator or auditor reads the README to learn how the control is evidenced
classification_rationale: Required-doc item 6: the sibling README states the response retention, the read-audit surfaces, the enable-audit verb, the disabled-state denial wording and the staggered-command window; this README stated none.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. The claims the README did make (#4990, #5261) were accurate.

trigger: a later fix to the path-under-network-mount test lands in one of three copies
classification_rationale: The prefix-containment predicate and the Data-volume alias logic now exist in three independent copies (this plugin, privacy_permissions macOS parsers, runtimes Linux parsers) with slightly different semantics; no routed clause names the path predicate as a single chokepoint, so no policy floor.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. The shared fstype list is already one copy. Hoisting the predicate is a new shared surface touching two other plugins.

trigger: 512 homes each holding two hostile 1 MiB authorized_keys files (or a root-set AuthorizedKeysFile that repeats)
classification_rationale: No total key-byte budget exists and the README stated only per-item caps; the true bound is 1,024 reads x 1 MiB on one shared worker with no execute deadline.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Also raised as sre-2 by the sre reviewer in the same review stage (two independent reporters). Measured 4.6-9.4 s CPU and IO on an M4, 30-40 s estimated on a cold disk; I5 only on pathological hardware, so the derived band is LOW.

trigger: the root filesystem itself is nfs4, 9p or virtiofs (NFS-root, Kata, some VM guests): the prefix '/' marks every path as network
classification_rationale: Config and every home are skipped with network_mount_skipped tokens; the behaviour is visible and fail-safe.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Probe verified with prefix '/'.

trigger: systemd is wedged (D-Bus hang): three units, 5 s deadline each, serial, no fail-fast after the first deadline
classification_rationale: About 15 s of one worker per dispatch with three subprocess_runner:deadline tokens; bounded and visible.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Default-off plugin, single-target dispatch.

trigger: write_output throws after rows have started (the execute_list catch arm appends a second status row)
classification_rationale: The YAML said 'leading status row'; only the README said the last status row wins; the typed UNAVAILABLE result is authoritative.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. The reporter's I3 reading is mitigated by the typed status, so the derived band is LOW.

trigger: the default two-entry AuthorizedKeysFile reaches kMaxKeyFileAttempts (1,024) at exactly 512 homes; 6,000 homes audit the first 512 in directory order
classification_rationale: The caps are documented in the README and visible (homes:too_many, keys:file_cap); homes are sorted so the audited set is deterministic.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Probe: 6,000 directories audit 512 with too_many.

trigger: a filesystem that reports DT_UNKNOWN (old XFS, some NFS/FUSE) lists plain files in /home as homes
classification_rationale: homes:enotdir failed rows and permanent CONSTRAINED noise for a regular file placed directly under a home root; honest and fail-safe.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. DT_UNKNOWN is kept deliberately so a refused symlinked home stays visible.

trigger: the kill switch is flipped off while a run is in flight or a delayed/staggered command already exists; an action-level ON row overrides a plugin-level OFF
classification_rationale: Platform behaviour shared by every kill-switched plugin: the switch is checked at dispatch only, most-specific scope wins, and the README did not say so.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Also raised as sre-3 (INFO) by the sre reviewer.

trigger: the Windows planned stub: return code 0 with a typed UNAVAILABLE status and one unsupported row, so automation keyed on the return code sees success
classification_rationale: The pattern exists across other planned stubs (shares, mgmt_posture); no workflow code reads the result status.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. The typed UNAVAILABLE status is the contract consumers key on.

trigger: an Administrator dispatches the plugin through /api/command while the seeded kill switch is OFF
classification_rationale: REST answers 403 'permission denied: Forensics:Read' to an Administrator who holds it, with no reason; MCP says 'an operator has thrown an emergency stop' for a default-off seed nobody threw. Shared dispatch code, identical for every default-off sibling.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Native MEDIUM; derived LOW (I8; I4 considered and rejected: diagnosable from the audit row and the README).

trigger: a customer reads the seeded kill-switch row through GET /api/v1/plugin-config/remote_access_audit/kill-switch
classification_rationale: The seeded reason string carried an internal programme label, which is customer-visible data.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Sibling plugins carry the same pattern from earlier programmes; the Architect ruled this PR's own string is dropped.

trigger: a regression in the production Paths wiring of run_macos or run_linux, or in macos_network_prefixes
classification_rationale: Eight macOS mutants (config path, home parent, min_uid 500 to 0, launchctl path and args, dropped fstype filter, dropped alias, launchd=false) all stayed green because the live dispatcher test is shape-only by design.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Ordinary missing coverage (SHOULD, not a floor). The uid-floor and path mutants need a uid-0 home or a seeded /etc/ssh, which the unit suites must not depend on; the Architect folded only the environment-stable wiring assertions.

trigger: a mount nested under a local home (for example /home/alice/.ssh on NFS)
classification_rationale: Removing the key-path mount guard stayed green in the legs and posix_fs tests; production code was correct.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. I5 on regression.

trigger: a malformed certificate body or an oversize modulus
classification_rationale: Certificate type 1/2, the 256-principal cap, CA-not-a-certificate, the signature type, critical-option and extension pairs, key_id and sk strings as C strings, and the 16384-bit cap each had no discriminating test; all fixtures were ed25519-CA user certificates.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. I3 on regression (a line sshd rejects listed as a key). A table-driven splice over the real certificate was recommended.

trigger: a key-file path leaking through a failure token or the status row
classification_rationale: The no-path-leak assertion covered only the config row, and has_token was a substring match, so appending the absolute path to the network_mount_skipped token stayed green.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. I1 on regression.

trigger: a root CI runner; readdir EIO during enumeration
classification_rationale: The unopenable-home test SKIPs visibly under euid 0, and the enumeration_error arms are untested (a fault-injected readdir does not belong in the unit suites).
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Visible SKIP is the shares precedent.

trigger: a reader of the committed macOS sample
classification_rationale: The sample carries the real SHA-256 fingerprint of a public key from the capture host (the account name is redacted); a fingerprint is not secret and the README standard requires an unedited real capture.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. The owner may still ask for anonymisation at the push gate.

trigger: /home is its own ext4 mount, so /home/lost+found (or any non-account directory) exists
classification_rationale: lost+found appears as an account row (file|lost+found|authorized_keys|absent) and is counted in the homes row; the Linux leg has no eligibility filter (macOS has the uid floor). Cosmetic.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Unprivileged agent: refused like every other home.

trigger: a second raw_digest() call, or hex_digest() after raw_digest(), on one Sha256 object
classification_rationale: raw_digest() finalises once and a second call is silently wrong (probe-verified); every caller is single-shot, which is why the wrong outcome cannot occur in production. The hex_digest behaviour is pre-existing; raw_digest is the newly public form.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Native INFO. The fix is a doc-comment line, not a guard.

trigger: new code uses int-errno returns and out-parameters where docs/cpp-conventions.md says to use std::expected
classification_rationale: Same shape as the merged shares plugin's posix binding, so it is the family idiom, not new drift; no catastrophic clause in the C++ conventions row, so no floor.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Static property of the code.

trigger: scripts/dev/check-windows-tu-syntax.sh lists only remote_access_audit_win.cpp, not the portable plugin TU
classification_rationale: Both TUs were compiled under mingw GCC with -fsyntax-only and are clean; the siblings (mgmt_posture, shares) list only their _win.cpp as well.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. The portable TU is compiled by the MSVC leg in CI.

trigger: a subject writes a key type token of up to 64 bytes of [A-Za-z0-9._@+-] followed by a blob that leads with that same string, in their own authorized_keys
classification_rationale: The subject-chosen text is echoed in the type field of a key row (bounded charset, pipe-safe); it is not a comment, option value or path. The reporter classified it n/a; recorded as absence because no document is wrong, the behaviour is accepted and bounded.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Noted because an agentic reader sees subject-chosen text in the type field.

trigger: a reader sees gather.ttlSeconds: 3600 and the README word 'TTL'
classification_rationale: The field is the agent response window, not a result cache (docs/yaml-dsl-spec.md); siblings use 300 and the definition test pins 3600.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. No stale identity-material cache exists; the wording invites a misreading.

trigger: a Windows installer build
classification_rationale: The installer lists neither privacy_permissions.dll nor browser_inventory.dll although their Windows legs ship; not caused by this change, which adds its own line beside mgmt_posture.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Verified by grep.

trigger: a PR raised without docs-unchanged lines: scripts/ci/check-plugin-readme-touch.sh exits 1 because the shared network_fstype hoist touches the runtimes and privacy_permissions parsers but not their READMEs
classification_rationale: The advisory job is not a required check; this plugin itself passes (src and README both changed).
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Closed by two visible docs-unchanged lines in the PR body; no code change.

trigger: a reader sees service|...|unknown
classification_rationale: On Linux unknown always accompanies a CONSTRAINED service token; on macOS it means a successful read with no launchd override entry and the status stays supported.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. One README clause.

trigger: a documented-but-never-emitted token goes unnoticed (doc-1 survived seven gates)
classification_rationale: The token vocabulary has no machine gate: agent.cpp stores provenance raw and plugin_doc_gen reads only descriptors, while update_source_trust has a token test.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. A small follow-up task, not part of this change.

trigger: a substring token assertion in the legs test
classification_rationale: keys:oversized also matches keys:oversized_line, and two assertions drop the <os>:remote_access_audit: prefix, so a wrong suffix passes.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Folded into the exact-token has_token of qe-4.

trigger: the dev back-merge of an identical-edit hunk in tests/test_capability_gate_consistency.py
classification_rationale: The feature commit body says 'effective sshd_config settings' (the product reports configured access); EXPECTED_TOTAL_ROWS goes 232 to 233 on this branch while dev is already at 233, so after the back-merge the total must read 234 and an auto-merged identical hunk can produce a wrong 233.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. History is never rewritten; the PR body is seeded from the README; the total is re-checked at the back-merge.

trigger: an operator meets a homes:<errno> token or the 4096-entry directory bound that the Result-status table does not name
classification_rationale: homes:eloop, enotdir, eio, enametoolong and errno_<n> and the kMaxDirEntries bound (homes:too_many, include:too_many) were not tabulated; the changelog also omitted the Linux-unprivileged reality. Also raised as doc-4.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Cheap documentation completeness.

trigger: ESC, VT, FS/GS/RS, NEL and U+2028/9 survive wire_field; distinct names collide (a\nb vs a b)
classification_rationale: No row or status forgery is possible (pipes, CR and LF are escaped; the server splits on newline only); the residual is terminal injection for a CLI reader, in the shared sanitiser every plugin uses.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. The escape-grammar decision is existing issue #5208.

trigger: EMFILE mid-walk; hostile config and key shapes; HA simultaneous seed boot; stored-row retention
classification_rationale: Four verified-correct behaviours recorded as INFO: EMFILE is failed (never absent); hostile shapes are contained (400k-iteration fuzz, 0 leaks); the seed is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; rows are retained 90 days with the Response:Read gap cited as #4990.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. No defect found; one combined row, as the Architect ruled them together.

trigger: an emergency kill-switch flip while a delayed or in-flight dispatch exists
classification_rationale: The switch is read per dispatch and fails closed, but the agent never re-checks: an in-flight list finishes and a staggered command runs after the flip; most-specific scope wins. Platform behaviour for every kill-switched plugin; the README documented enabling only.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. The README sentence landed with comp-3.

trigger: a customer reads the Linux sample
classification_rationale: The Linux sample is a euid-0 container capture with test fixtures and shows 12 of 47 rows, none a key row; the macOS sample is euid 501 while the shipped macOS identity is root. Both are labelled with euid and container.
summary: Round-1 governance finding, recorded at the Gate 8 re-review from the round-1 report and sub-reports. Neither shows the real common outcome (all file rows refused); a refused-everything capture needs an unprivileged Linux agent on a multi-user host.

Fixed in de6ae4a51 (governance round 1 gate-fix; Architect ruling: adopted). Presence-only token <os>:remote_access_audit:sshd_config:other_credential_sources at global scope (Include'd files count, Match-scoped does not) for TrustedUserCAKeys, AuthorizedKeysCommand, AuthorizedPrincipalsFile, AuthorizedPrincipalsCommand, AuthenticationMethods and HostbasedAuthentication; the first occurrence decides and the keyword's disabling value (none / any / no, checked against servconf.c) is inert; no value or path reaches a row (asserted). README 'What it does not read' and the YAML description and header state the limit. The closure test asserts the wire (status constrained and the exact token) for all six keywords, the macOS prefix, an Include path and the controls. Gate 8 re-verification at f4445817e: held. code, tests and docs hold; 21 of 22 scratch mutants turn the closure test red, and the one inert literal no test exercises (TrustedUserCAKeys none) is raised as g8-va-1. Completeness of the closed set is a separate Gate 8 finding (g8-sg-1, GSSAPIAuthentication).

Fixed in de6ae4a51 (Architect ruling: adapted). As ruled, no presence token (the macOS Shared directory is owned by uid 0 on every Mac). trigger: a global GSSAPIAuthentication yes (own file or an Include'd file) on a host where every other read succeeds (a macOS root agent, or a Linux agent that is root or holds the ambient capability)
classification_rationale: README 'What it does not read' lists the login sources the plugin never opens and omits Kerberos/GSSAPI, and the YAML header and description say 'one of these six'; the listing is presented as supported with no token and no config row for a login source that needs no key. Required-doc item 6 (the plugin README is the routed row's update obligation).
summary: Gate 8 governance finding (re-review of the range after round 1). kOtherCredentialKeys holds six entries (TrustedUserCAKeys, AuthorizedKeysCommand, AuthorizedPrincipalsFile, AuthorizedPrincipalsCommand, AuthenticationMethods, HostbasedAuthentication) and GSSAPIAuthentication is not one of them; a compiled probe over a copy of the HEAD headers gave status|list|supported|- with no token for 'GSSAPIAuthentication yes', while PasswordAuthentication, KbdInteractiveAuthentication, UsePAM, PermitEmptyPasswords and PubkeyAuthentication each produce a config row. A scratch copy with the seventh keyword agrees with sshd -T on 2,827 generated configs. The RHEL-family stock default of yes is from memory and not re-verified. Same defect class as hp-1: the closure in the round-1 fix left the set incomplete. Minimal fold: add {gssapiauthentication, no} to the closed set and extend the README (What it does not read and the Result-status row), the YAML header and description, the definition-test phrase 'one of these six', the descriptor notes and the wire-test table, with a mutation. The alternative is an owner-recorded acceptance under 'NOT read, and NOT detectable'. Native label MEDIUM; the derived band governs. Design caution for the ruling: the RHEL-family stock configuration sets GSSAPIAuthentication yes globally (50-redhat.conf, per the RHEL 10 STIG listing; the RHEL 9 STIG check implies the same default), so flagging every global yes would leave a stock RHEL-family host permanently constrained even after the capability grant. Options: flag only when /etc/krb5.keytab exists (mgmt_posture already tests it), flag every yes, or record the gap as NOT read and NOT detectable. Until folded, a clean supported listing must not be cited as the complete SSH access population (compliance-officer note).

summary: Gate 8 governance finding (re-review of the range after round 1). Also raised independently by consistency-auditor, enterprise-readiness, verifier B. The ponytail-review round-8 trim (ruling RAA-docs-8, 'drop the rest') cut the fragment from 1,663 to 813 bytes; its stated reason names only the symlink and mount sentence and the walked-roots detail. Proposed fold (about 330 bytes, in line with the shares and mgmt_posture fragments): replace 'in each account's authorized_keys' with 'in the authorized_keys of each home it walks' and add a sentence that it is not the whole answer to who can log in: a host whose sshd_config sets a certificate authority, a key or principals command or file, host-based authentication or AuthenticationMethods is reported as constrained, and the Linux leg, which runs unprivileged and usually cannot open other users' homes, is declared constrained. Round-1 xplat-2 and doc-3 are re-opened on the same fact. House standard (enterprise-readiness): sibling fragments run 873 to 1,111 bytes and state the unreadable-source outcome (mgmt_posture), that stored results are readable by Response:Read holders (shares) and the unmeasured root-daemon outcome (privacy_permissions); add the Response:Read clause too. trigger: systemctl is-enabled writes any stderr line beside the answer, for example a unit with no native unit file but an /etc/init.d script under systemd 257 or earlier (SysV redirect lines)
classification_rationale: Merged stderr turns a correct enabled or disabled answer into service:unrecognised_output (constrained, unknown rows) because stdout is block-buffered on a pipe, so every stderr line lands before the answer; fake-stderr probes verified the parse effect. Not shown for ssh.service, sshd.service or ssh.socket on the captured Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04 hosts (native units, merged output exactly enabled / alias / disabled, even with /etc/init.d/ssh present); only a SysV-only sshd would hit it, which is rare and unverified on a real host.
summary: Gate 8 governance finding (re-review of the range after round 1). Fail-safe (honest unknown, flagged constrained, never a wrong state). Accept; optional fold: take the first line that is an exact state word and keep the exact not-found rule, plus one clause in the sink manifest.

trigger: an sshd_config edited into a shape sshd refuses (AuthorizedKeysFile none x, HostbasedAuthentication true, a BOM) without a reload
classification_rationale: The parser is lenient or conservative on configs sshd would refuse to load (AuthorizedKeysFile 'none' among other tokens is rejected whole and the default entries are listed with no token; HostbasedAuthentication true or off is flagged though sshd rejects it); it matters only if the running daemon predates the edit, and the plugin reports configured facts. A differential of 52 hand-built shapes against sshd -T (OpenSSH 10.3) agrees on every config sshd accepts except the known Match all.
summary: Gate 8 governance finding (re-review of the range after round 1). Accept.

classification_rationale: A prefix with a trailing slash never matches its children, and /System/Volumes/Data/ yields the alias / (deny-all, fail-safe); mountinfo field 5 and getmntinfo f_mntonname never carry a trailing slash, so production sources cannot produce the case (unit level only).
summary: Gate 8 governance finding (re-review of the range after round 1). Accept.
